newsitem.title: UK: Surcharge end makes way for higher ex-UK cargo rate.
newsitem.headline: Surcharge end makes way for higher ex-UK cargo rate.

text.p: A sudden rush to scrap surcharges in the past few days has made it easier for airlines to justify higher tariffs being introduced at the start of this month when summer schedules were introduced, a Reuters survey showed.

Most carriers are removing surcharges with effect from April 15 and on Thursday Lufthansa the world's largest international freight carrier said it was doing so on a global basis made. Once this happened most other carriers operating out of the UK did likewise. The notable exception was British Airways who late on Friday was still keeping its surcharge in place.

Most freight forwarders and airline sources said it can only be a matter of days before all carriers fall into line removing their surcharges as jet fuel prices are back to the levels of last July, or earlier, depending on how the comparison is made.

What is clear is that most sections of the air cargo industry have spent time over the past six months building a better dialogue between the different sectors so that surcharges are not again suddenly introduced without warning.
Most carriers are increasing capacity in the summer schedules and as a result many industry sources are wary of predicting continued firmness in rates.
But two factors are helping keep demand buoyant for westbound air freight from the UK. Firstly for the N Atlantic the strength of the dollar is keeping import demand high.

Another factor which put a squeeze on widebodied cargo space is the decision by American Airlines to replace Boeing 767-200 on its four times daily New York and once daily Boston passenger flights with refurbished Airbus A300-600.

The Airbuses have improved inflight entertainment but until pilots become more familiar with the Airbus, the carrier is being cautious at the tonnage it is prepared to lift, said John Smith its managing director for European cargo sales.
"On some of the early flights we had to keep the (uplift) weight down as we had severe headwinds," he added.
American will have a reduced capacity with the Airbus but in the long-term a new wage deal with its pilots will allow it to go ahead with its plans for larger planes.
Overall last month American Airlines on all its systems carried a record tonnage for March beating expectations, Smith added.
American have yet to announced a removal of surcharge but a decision is likely early next week Smith said pointing out it was not amongst the first to introduce one in November.

United Airlines' Peter Chase said the timing of a rate increase originally planned for January and the removal of surcharges - which it removed with effect April 7 - meant that the net impact on its customers was for a small reduction on the bottom line.
UAL had raised rates by an average five percent but the removal of the fuel surcharge took five to ten percent off freight costs, Chase said.
Steve Lewis of Polar Air Cargo also reported good business ex-UK over the Atlantic of a fairly general nature with shipments of show-jumping and eventing horses providing some added interest.

Peter Brooks of Cargolink also reported a good general level of business. Cargolink runs a leased freighter on a wet lease from Bridgetown to Santiago, Lima, Caracas and Buenos Aires taking cargo mainly carried from the UK in the bellyholds of BA charter. Brooks said recent cargo featured car and computer components and telecoummication systems, especially for Peru.

Peter Simmonds UK cargo sales and services manager for TWA said that overall the N Atlantic market had quietened since Easter but had been supported by American Airlines' switch to A300's. Cargoes flown by TWA included the fairly typical electronic and aircraft parts but recently it carried more leisure items like CD's and sunglasses

Iberia Airlines' Enrique Sagra said business to Buenos Aires in the coming week is featured the carrying of grand prix racing cars to the seond major motor race of the 1997 season. , Sagra said he had been asked to carry 50 tonnes of racing cargo in a special joint 747 freighter flight with Aerolineas Argentinas leaving Stansted for Buenos Aires via Maastricht.

Simon Allsop of general service agents Air Cargo partners whose clients include Polar Air Cargo, said reduced 747 freighter capacity was holding rates firm and Polar's space was sometimes booked upto two weeks ahead.
From this week Reuters is quoting the ex-UK rate to Caracas at 1.30 stg a kilo for a 100 kilo shipment. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
